This name is associated with the God Ashtavakra, who was born free from the physical and mental afflictions. Parents who choose Asav usually hope their child will grow to embody free from and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_sanskrit.name: असव:
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The Sanskrit word 'असव:' (Asav) is derived from the prefix 'अस-' (as) which means 'not' and the suffix 'व-' (v) which denotes absence. It can be interpreted as 'absence of', 'not present', or 'lack of'. In Hindu mythology, the demon Asura (असुर) is also called Asava (असव) because he was the embodiment of 'asav' or absence of divine qualities.

data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the name Asav carries deep spiritual significance as it embodies the concept of ‘moksha’ or liberation from the cycle of birth and rebirth.
